title: Children's ENT checkup
also: kids ear nose and throat doctor
what: An ENT doctor examines your child's ears, nose, and throat. The exam is usually short and does not hurt.
why: For frequent colds and ear infections, snoring, mouth breathing, ear or throat pain, poor hearing, and routine checkups.
tell_doctor: How often your child gets ill, and with what
If they snore or breathe through the mouth
How they hear and speak for their age
What medicines and drops you have already given

prepare.title: Talk to your child
prepare.text: Tell your child the doctor will look at their ears and throat with a little flashlight.

prepare.title: Timing
prepare.text: Best to come when your child is not hungry or sleepy.

bring: Past medical reports and test results
steps: Your child sits on your lap, and you gently hold them
The doctor checks the throat with a tongue depressor
The nose and ears are examined
The doctor explains what was found and gives treatment
feel: The tongue depressor may cause gagging
Little ones often cry from being held. That is normal
after: Come back for a follow-up if the doctor says so
red_flags: Your child has trouble breathing, cannot swallow, or is drooling: call emergency services
High fever and severe ear pain, or swelling behind the ear: see a doctor urgently

faq.q: Do adenoids need to be removed if my child snores?
faq.a: Not always. The doctor will examine your child and say what they need.

faq.q: How do I hold my child during the exam?
faq.a: Sit them on your lap. Wrap one arm around their body and arms, and hold their head with the other hand.

reminders.text: Your child's ENT checkup is in 2 hours. Bring past medical reports.
